description: Requirement-level inventory of every BCP 14 statement in the pinned supported CloudEvents core, JSON format, HTTP binding, Kafka binding, distributed-tracing subset, and partitioning extension. Conformance-boilerplate keyword definitions are excluded; keyword_lines provides a machine-checkable occurrence inventory.

requirements.text: Implementations supporting an encoding MUST adhere to that event format's encoding rules.
All implementations MUST support the JSON format.
An OPTIONAL feature is OPTIONAL for both producer and consumer.
requirements.limitation: This defines how specification options are interpreted; it is not a package behavior.

requirements.text: An intermediary SHOULD forward OPTIONAL attributes.
A single occurrence MAY result in more than one event.
requirements.limitation: Occurrence-to-event cardinality is chosen by producers.

requirements.text: Protocol bindings MAY define protocol-dependent formats.
requirements.limitation: This permission applies to protocol-binding specifications, not this implementation.

requirements.text: Protocol bindings MAY map an event format directly to the envelope body or MAY add formatting and structure.
Every CloudEvent MUST contain REQUIRED context attributes and MAY contain OPTIONAL and extension attributes.
Attribute names MUST contain only lower-case ASCII letters or digits.
Attribute names SHOULD be descriptive and terse and SHOULD NOT exceed 20 characters.
requirements.limitation: The stable v1.0.2 validity rule permits longer names; the package bounds them by configurable resource limits rather than rejecting names over 20 characters.

requirements.text: Formats MAY represent abstract types differently, but every implementation MUST support each canonical string encoding.
Event formats MUST use Integer values only in the signed 32-bit range.
All context attribute values MUST use a CloudEvents abstract type.
Attribute values MAY be represented as native types or canonical strings.
A strongly typed model MUST convert between canonical strings and corresponding native types.
requirements.limitation: Typed attributes have native constructors and format or binding decoders accept canonical strings, but the public strongly typed Attribute API does not expose canonical-string constructors for every abstract type.

requirements.text: Timestamp values MUST be settable from RFC 3339 strings and MUST convert to RFC 3339 strings for protocol metadata.
requirements.limitation: Timestamp decoding accepts RFC 3339 and encoding returns RFC 3339, but the public timestamp constructor accepts time.Time rather than an RFC 3339 string.

requirements.text: A protocol binding or event format implementation MUST convert between canonical string encodings and corresponding encoded types.
The id, source, specversion, and type attributes are REQUIRED in every CloudEvent.
Producers MUST ensure source plus id is unique for each distinct event.
requirements.limitation: Cross-event producer uniqueness cannot be established by a value codec.

requirements.text: A retransmitted duplicate MAY reuse id, and consumers MAY treat identical source plus id values as duplicates.
requirements.limitation: Retry identity and deduplication are caller-owned policies.

requirements.text: id is REQUIRED.
id MUST be a non-empty string.
id MUST be unique within the producer's scope.
requirements.limitation: The package has no producer identity store.

requirements.text: Producers MUST ensure source plus id is unique for each distinct event.
requirements.limitation: Cross-event producer uniqueness cannot be established by a value codec.

requirements.text: An application MAY assign each producer a unique source and MAY use UUIDs, URNs, DNS authorities, or an application-specific scheme.
requirements.limitation: Source assignment is caller-owned.

requirements.text: A source MAY contain multiple producers; those producers MUST collaborate to keep source plus id unique.
requirements.limitation: Producer coordination is outside the package.

requirements.text: source is REQUIRED.
source MUST be a non-empty URI-reference.
An absolute source URI is RECOMMENDED.
requirements.limitation: Relative URI-references are valid and source selection belongs to the producer.

requirements.text: Compliant producers MUST use specversion 1.0 for this specification version.
specversion is REQUIRED.
specversion MUST be a non-empty string.
type is REQUIRED.
type MUST be a non-empty string.
type SHOULD use a reverse-DNS prefix.
requirements.limitation: The recommendation governs producer naming and is not a validity constraint.

requirements.text: datacontenttype, dataschema, subject, and time are OPTIONAL.
An event format MAY omit datacontenttype when it defines an implied content type.
When translating an event with implied datacontenttype, the target SHOULD set that type explicitly.
datacontenttype is OPTIONAL.
When present, datacontenttype MUST be an RFC 2046 media type.
Incompatible schema changes SHOULD use a different dataschema URI.
requirements.limitation: Schema versioning is owned by event producers and schema publishers.

requirements.text: dataschema is OPTIONAL.
When present, dataschema MUST be a non-empty URI.
subject is OPTIONAL.
When present, subject MUST be a non-empty string.
A producer MAY substitute another time when occurrence time is unknown, but producers sharing a source MUST use a consistent policy.
requirements.limitation: Timestamp selection and cross-producer consistency are caller-owned.

requirements.text: time is OPTIONAL.
When present, time MUST follow RFC 3339.
A CloudEvent MAY contain distinct extension attributes; extensions MUST follow core naming and type-system rules.
An extension with a secondary transport mapping SHOULD define how receivers handle conflicting copied values.
requirements.limitation: This governs extension specification authors.

requirements.text: An extension definition SHOULD fully define each attribute.
requirements.limitation: This governs extension specification authors.

requirements.text: New extension definitions SHOULD use descriptive collision-resistant names.
requirements.limitation: This governs extension specification authors.

requirements.text: Extension authors SHOULD check the documented-extension registry.
requirements.limitation: This governs extension specification authors.

requirements.text: Receivers are RECOMMENDED to preserve non-CloudEvents protocol metadata through a distinguishable mechanism.
requirements.limitation: Kafka decoding returns unowned transport headers; HTTP decoding intentionally does not return unrelated HTTP headers.

requirements.text: A CloudEvent MAY contain domain-specific event data.
Event data is OPTIONAL.
Applications crossing encodings or protocols SHOULD account for the least efficient representation.
requirements.limitation: Routing topology and protocol selection are caller-owned.

requirements.text: Intermediaries MUST forward events of 64 KByte or less.
requirements.limitation: The module is a codec and does not operate an intermediary.

requirements.text: Consumers SHOULD accept events of at least 64 KByte.
Publishers SHOULD keep events compact and link to large data instead of embedding it.
requirements.limitation: Payload design is caller-owned.

requirements.text: Sensitive information SHOULD NOT be carried in context attributes.
requirements.limitation: The generic model cannot identify sensitive values; selected adapters apply explicit trust and audit policies.

requirements.text: Producers, consumers, and intermediaries MAY inspect and log context attributes.
requirements.limitation: The package performs no logging.

requirements.text: Domain event data SHOULD be encrypted to restrict visibility to trusted parties.
requirements.limitation: Payload encryption is an agreement between producer and consumer.

requirements.text: Protocol-level security SHOULD protect CloudEvents in transit.
requirements.limitation: The transport-neutral codecs do not establish network connections.

requirements.text: Extension attributes MUST be serialized as top-level JSON properties.
The CloudEvents type system MUST map to the specified JSON types.
Unset attributes MAY be encoded as JSON null.
requirements.limitation: The encoder omits unset attributes; the decoder accepts null as permitted.

requirements.text: A null attribute value MUST be treated as unset or omitted.
Extension specifications MAY add secondary JSON mappings but MUST retain the primary mapping.
requirements.limitation: This governs extension specification authors.

requirements.text: A secondary JSON mapping MUST define mappings for every other core event format.
requirements.limitation: This governs extension specification authors.

requirements.text: A JSON event representation MUST use application/cloudevents+json.
Every REQUIRED and present OPTIONAL attribute MUST become a correctly named and typed JSON object member.
A present OPTIONAL attribute MAY be represented by JSON null.
requirements.limitation: Encoding uses the equivalent omission form.

requirements.text: A JSON serializer MUST first determine the runtime data type.
Binary data MUST be a Base64 JSON string in data_base64.
When present for binary data, datacontenttype MUST describe the original binary format.
requirements.limitation: The package preserves an explicit media type and reports implicit representation changes.

requirements.text: Absent datacontenttype SHOULD be processed as application/json.
JSON-formatted data MUST be translated to data and stored directly as a JSON value.
Serialization MAY fail when runtime data cannot be translated to JSON.
Non-JSON text data MUST be stored as a correctly encoded string in data.
Serialization MAY fail when a runtime value cannot be represented as a correctly encoded string.
JSON-formatted data MAY contain any JSON value, including explicit null distinct from absent data.
data_base64 MUST decode to binary runtime data and MAY be interpreted further using datacontenttype.
requirements.limitation: The package returns owned binary bytes and does not perform optional media-type-specific interpretation.

requirements.text: JSON-formatted data MUST be treated directly as a JSON value.
A JSON string data value MUST remain a string and MUST NOT be reparsed as a JSON document.
Non-JSON data SHOULD be an encoded content string; decoding MAY fail for a non-string or uninterpretable value.
When datacontenttype is absent, a data member SHOULD be processed directly as application/json.
When converting implicit JSON data to another format or binding, datacontenttype SHOULD be set explicitly to application/json.
JSON Batch MUST NOT be used when only JSON Event Format support was indicated.
requirements.limitation: The codec exposes batch as a distinct explicit mode; negotiation remains caller-owned.

requirements.text: A JSON batch MUST use application/cloudevents-batch+json.
A compliant HTTP implementation SHOULD support structured and binary modes.
Structured mode MUST support non-batch JSON and MAY support additional formats.
requirements.limitation: Only JSON event and JSON batch formats are implemented.

requirements.text: Event formats MAY define a batch representation for HTTP batch mode.
Batch mode MUST NOT be used unless solicited, and solicitation SHOULD let the receiver choose a maximum batch size.
requirements.limitation: The explicit BatchMode codec has no negotiation layer; callers own solicitation and negotiated size.

requirements.text: A receiver MAY treat an unsupported structured event format as binary and forward it unchanged.
requirements.limitation: The package elects the other permitted behavior and returns ErrUnsupportedMode.

requirements.text: In binary mode, HTTP Content-Type MUST map to datacontenttype.
Binary mode MUST NOT also carry ce-datacontenttype.
Every non-data attribute, including extensions, MUST map individually to a distinct HTTP header.
Extensions MAY define secondary HTTP mappings, but the primary ce- mapping MUST remain present.
requirements.limitation: No specialized secondary HTTP mappings are emitted.

requirements.text: Context attributes MUST map to ce- followed by the attribute name.
HTTP header values MUST use printable US-ASCII and may have OPTIONAL surrounding whitespace after CRLF.
String attribute header values MUST be percent-encoded once and SHOULD NOT be further encoded.
Inbound attribute header values MUST be unescaped as quoted strings and then percent-decoded exactly once.
Receivers MUST accept legacy double-quoted attribute header values.
A Unicode surrogate pair MUST be treated as one Unicode character.
requirements.limitation: Go strings are processed as UTF-8 bytes after scalar-value validation; valid supplementary characters round-trip as one UTF-8 sequence.

requirements.text: Space, double quote, percent, and non-printable-ASCII characters MUST be percent-encoded.
Header encoders are RECOMMENDED to percent-encode prohibited control characters defensively.
requirements.limitation: The event model rejects prohibited controls before encoding and the encoder percent-encodes every byte outside printable ASCII.

requirements.text: Percent encoding SHOULD use uppercase hex; decoders MUST accept lowercase hex.
Decoders MUST accept unnecessary percent encoding and MUST reject invalid UTF-8 encoded byte sequences, including overlong forms.
The normative Unicode example SHOULD encode space, euro, and emoji using the specified UTF-8 percent sequences.
Structured HTTP Content-Type MUST be an event-format media type.
Structured mode MAY repeat binary-mode ce- headers.
requirements.limitation: The encoder omits redundant headers; the decoder accepts matching copies and rejects conflicts.

requirements.text: All CloudEvents metadata MUST remain in the structured payload even when repeated in HTTP headers.
The event format used in batch mode MUST define a batch representation.
Every compliant implementation MUST support JSON Batch for HTTP batch mode.
Batched HTTP Content-Type MUST be an event-format media type.
An HTTP batch MAY be empty and every event in it MUST share specversion.
Other attributes in an HTTP batch MAY differ, including datacontenttype.
Users SHOULD configure record key or partition according to their application.
requirements.limitation: Topic partitioning policy is caller-owned.

requirements.text: The binding provides an OPTIONAL record-key mapping without requiring its use.
Binary mode MUST place data bytes unchanged in the record value and MUST map every other attribute to headers.
Kafka 0.11 or newer MAY use binary or structured mode; older Kafka MUST use structured JSON.
requirements.limitation: The transport-neutral record codec targets header-capable Kafka records and does not negotiate broker versions.

requirements.text: Structured Kafka implementations MUST support JSON event format.
A receiver MAY treat an unsupported structured event format as binary and forward it unchanged.
requirements.limitation: The package elects the other permitted behavior and returns ErrUnsupportedMode.

requirements.text: By default, an implementation MUST copy the user-provided record key to the Kafka record key.
A key mapper MAY populate the record key from event or application information.
requirements.limitation: KafkaPartitionKey supplies the selected event-attribute mapper; arbitrary mapping can be applied by the caller before encoding.

requirements.text: An implementation SHOULD offer an opt-in mapper from partitionkey to record key unchanged.
A key mapper MUST NOT modify the CloudEvent, MUST retain partitionkey in the event, and MUST NOT add out-of-band key data as an attribute.
Binary Kafka content-type MUST map directly to datacontenttype.
Binary data bytes MUST be the Kafka record value.
Every non-data attribute MUST map individually to Kafka headers, and keys and values MUST be UTF-8 strings.
When present in structured mode, content-type MUST identify an event format.
Structured mode MAY repeat binary-mode Kafka headers.
requirements.limitation: The encoder omits redundant headers; the decoder accepts matching copies and rejects conflicts.

requirements.text: When the distributed-tracing extension is used, traceparent is REQUIRED.
tracestate is OPTIONAL.
For a single-hop transmission, the extension MUST carry the same trace information as protocol-specific tracing headers.
requirements.limitation: Equality is established only when callers use the explicit Golib propagation-policy adapter; core codecs do not inspect protocol-specific trace headers.

requirements.text: For a multi-hop transmission, the extension MUST retain the starting trace.
requirements.limitation: The stateless codecs cannot identify the starting hop; callers must preserve the original extension.

requirements.text: The extension MUST NOT be rewritten with trace information for each individual hop.
requirements.limitation: The stateless codecs neither create spans nor control intermediary rewriting.

requirements.text: When the partitioning extension is used, partitionkey is REQUIRED.
partitionkey MUST be a non-empty string.

unsupported_surfaces.limitation: No Avro parser, serializer, schema registration, or media-type implementation is exposed.
No Protobuf parser, serializer, schema registration, or media-type implementation is exposed.
No AMQP binding or adapter is exposed.
No MQTT binding or adapter is exposed.
No NATS binding or adapter is exposed.
No WebSockets binding or adapter is exposed.
Generic attribute retention is not dataref dereference, integrity, lifetime, or claim-check semantics.
Generic attribute retention is not sampling-rate validation or sampling policy.
Generic attribute retention is not sequence validation, ordering, wraparound, or gap semantics.
